Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as … as conjunction

also as much as, as many as, as … as possible, so … as, as big as

classical

Catull. 3.6–7: suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem

tam … quam

adverb and conjunction, with adjectives and adverbs

Tam goes with the adjective or adverb, quam introduces the other term, in the same case: tam bene quam puella.

Other words

  • tantus … quantus (tantum … quantum, tot … quot) — as big as, as much as, as many as

    correlative pronouns and adverbs: size, amount and number · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.2.1: quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās

    For size tantus … quantus, for amount tantum … quantum, for number tot … quot; the quantus-clause may come first.

  • quam (+ superlative) — as … as possible

    quam with a superlative adjective or adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 6.7.3: tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe; Cato Agr. 66: quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat · Wiktionary

    Quam prīmum, as soon as possible; quam plūrimī, as many as possible.

Examples

  • nam mellītus erat suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem

    for he was sweet as honey, and knew his mistress as well as a little girl knows her motherCatull. 3.6–7

  • quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās

    as much as you love me, so much see that you get wellCic. Fam. 16.2.1

  • tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe

    all the same, do write as often as you canPlin. Ep. 6.7.3

  • quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat

    let it be done as cleanly and purely as possibleCato Agr. 66

  • aut quam sīdera multa, cum tacet nox

    or as many as the stars, when the night is silentCatull. 7.7

See also than, as, same, so big!, the more …, the more ….
